assets.label: export transfer pumps
assets.service: tank-to-jetty product transfer, same seal class as the Marrindal family

control_failures.control_label: secondary containment by bund and drainage
controlled transfer of hydrocarbon between vessels
integrity of the mechanical seal support system

facts.title: residual pressure found after isolation of P-7111

response.consequence: The recorded outcome was lost time injury, with 1 person injured and 4 days lost. The potential outcome was rated 5 against the site's consequence scale, above the 3 actually realised.

defences.finding: Control BUND_AND_DRAINAGE_CONTAINMENT: the secondary containment by bund and drainage was in place but did not perform, and the accident investigation classified this as a task or environmental condition.
Control HYDROCARBON_TRANSFER_CONTROL: the controlled transfer of hydrocarbon between vessels had been bypassed, and the accident investigation classified this as an organisational factor.

Control SEAL_SUPPORT_SYSTEM_INTEGRITY: the integrity of the mechanical seal support system had degraded below its design intent, and the accident investigation classified this as an individual or team action.

recommendations: Confirm at the next spot check that the secondary containment by bund and drainage on P-7111, M-7111 and TK-7102 performs as designed.
response.sequence: Work was under way in managing hydrocarbon transfer and storage, specifically bunding, drainage and spill containment. P-7111 (export transfer pumps) is in service for tank-to-jetty product transfer, same seal class as the Marrindal family. The task proceeded during shift handover while the secondary containment by bund and drainage was in place but did not perform. The thermal energy involved is held as hot surface, and the recorded presentation was burn, ignition, scald.
response.summary: On 2 June 2005 a near hit was recorded on P-7111, M-7111 and TK-7102 at Cape Verity Export Terminal during shift handover; thermal energy held as hot surface was not released.
